strengths: Introduces a novel and practical panoramic equirectangular representation as a 2D-3D interface for 3D visual grounding, avoiding explicit view-direction prediction while retaining 360-degree object-to-object spatial context.

The three-stage pipeline is clearly presented: structure-aware camera placement, multi-modal panoramic rendering with semantic/geometric features, VLM grounding, and visibility-aware 3D lifting/fusion. The overall architecture is coherent and well motivated.

The multi-modal feature adapter with zero-initialized injection into the VLM is a sensible way to introduce 3D-aware cues without destroying pretrained VLM representations, and the EMD loss plus geometric QA provide useful auxiliary supervision.
Empirical evidence is strong: state-of-the-art or highly competitive results on ScanRefer, Nr3D, and Sr3D, with notable gains on multiple-object splits and human-written Nr3D queries.

Generalization experiments are compelling, showing smaller degradation on unseen ARKitScenes and 3RScan scenes, as well as improved robustness to LLaMA-generated text variants, especially when class names are removed.
The panorama-vs-pinhole comparison is a particularly informative analysis, demonstrating that the panoramic representation captures scene context beyond what narrow field-of-view views can provide.
The supplementary material adds useful implementation details, runtime analysis, camera placement ablations, 3DGS-vs-mesh comparison, and qualitative results, improving reproducibility and clarity.
The paper is generally well written and the figures/tables communicate the method and results effectively.
weaknesses: The method relies on equirectangular panoramas but does not analyze the impact of severe spherical distortion on the VLM or on SAM-based mask lifting. Since both CogVLM and SAM are pretrained on pinhole images, grounding and segmentation near the poles or on distorted object shapes may be brittle, yet no failure analysis or distortion-aware design is provided.

Applicability depends on access to original RGB views and camera poses for semantic feature lifting, and on camera trajectory proximity for camera placement. For 3D datasets available only as cleaned point clouds or meshes without capture metadata, the proposed pipeline may degrade or not apply directly.

The core ablations show only modest and sometimes non-monotonic gains: adding geometric features without QA slightly hurts relative to semantic-only (60.4 to 60.2), and the full model improves over semantic-only by only 0.6 Acc@0.25. The significance of the geometric branch and auxiliary objectives is therefore somewhat overstated relative to the dominant effect of the VLM and semantic features.

Fair-comparison nuances remain. In the GT-segmentation setting, PanoGrounder is below PQ3D on original ScanRefer and rephrased queries, so the text-robustness claim is subtler than the main text suggests. Some baselines are re-run while others are not, and differences in backbone scale and pretraining data complicate direct comparison.

The limitations discussion is brief and mostly future-work oriented. There is little concrete error analysis, no discussion of heavy 17B-model computational cost and LoRA fine-tuning requirements, and no broader societal-impact discussion.

Some components are underspecified, such as the denoising step in visibility-aware aggregation and how robust the two-stage ReferIt3D variant is to poor 2D masks or view selection failures. These details matter for reproducibility and real-world reliability.

strengths: Proposes panoramic multi-modal renderings as a 2D-3D interface for VLM-based 3D visual grounding, with a clear motivation: preserving 360-degree object-to-object relations while leveraging 2D VLM language reasoning.

Reports strong empirical results on ScanRefer and Nr3D, with particularly large gains on Nr3D and on multiple-object splits, and provides generalization experiments on unseen datasets and text rephrasings.
Includes useful ablations on camera placement, input modalities, EMD loss, geometric QA, test-time augmentation, and mesh vs. 3DGS representation, giving some insight into design choices.
The overall pipeline is reasonably clear and practical, with runtime analysis and support for both mesh and 3D Gaussian Splatting scene representations.
weaknesses: Fairness of the main SOTA comparisons is questionable: the method uses a 17B CogVLM pretrained on massive image-text data plus DINOv2/SAM, while many baselines are trained from scratch on 3D data. The claim of not leveraging additional large-scale datasets ignores the web-scale pretraining of the VLM backbone.

The generalization experiments rely on ground-truth object segmentation/proposals, so they test candidate selection/language robustness rather than end-to-end generalization. The abstract overstates generalization to unseen 3D datasets and rephrasings.

Several key implementation details are missing or underspecified, hurting reproducibility: how training 2D boxes are derived from instance-ID maps, how test-time augmented predictions are aggregated, how point clouds are denoised, how the two-stage matching/voting works, and the preprocessing cost of camera placement.

The EMD loss formulation is technically questionable. With place-value weights such as 10^2 for the hundreds digit and lambda=10, the EMD term would be expected to dominate cross-entropy, which is inconsistent with the reported training curves; digits are modeled independently, so it is not a true coordinate-level EMD. Its ablation gain is also small.

Necessity of several components is not strongly established. Geometric features alone reduce accuracy in the ablation, and the full model improves only marginally over semantic+QA variants. There are no repeated runs or error bars, making small gains unconvincing.

Panoramic distortion is not addressed. Equirectangular images have severe distortion, yet the method relies on LoRA/adapter fine-tuning without spherical-aware modeling or analysis showing the VLM actually reasons over panoramas rather than adapting to the fine-tuned domain.

The method depends on original posed RGB views to build the semantic feature field, which limits applicability to arbitrary 3D scenes or 3DGS reconstructions without such views. This requirement is not stated in the problem setup.

Baseline re-runs and reported numbers are insufficiently justified. For example, some Table 2 results differ dramatically from Table 1 under GT masks, and the 'fair comparison' protocol lacks enough detail to verify.

The SOTA claim is somewhat overstated: on Sr3D the method is not best, and on ScanRefer the best numbers in generalization/text tables use GT segmentation, making them not directly comparable to the main full-pipeline results.
Failure analysis and limitations are limited. There is little discussion of SAM failures, aggregation failure modes, computational cost of preprocessing/fine-tuning, or societal impact.

strengths: The paper introduces a novel and effective 2D-3D interface for VLM-based 3D visual grounding: panoramic equirectangular renderings preserve 360-degree scene context and long-range object relations while remaining directly compatible with a pretrained VLM.

The proposed pipeline is well designed and reasonably modular: structure-aware camera placement, multi-modal panoramas (RGB, semantic, range), zero-convolution adapters for feature injection, and visibility-aware multi-view lifting/fusion.

The empirical results are strong: state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance on ScanRefer and Nr3D, with especially clear gains on the challenging Multiple/human-annotated splits and on text generalization.

Generalization analysis is a major strength. Cross-dataset evaluation on ARKitScenes+SceneVerse and 3RScan+RIORefer, plus four text perturbations, supports the claim that the method transfers better than prior supervised baselines.

The supplement is thorough and useful: additional ablations on camera placement, test-time augmentation, adapter initialization, mesh vs. 3DGS, runtime, prompts, and training details increase confidence in the method.
Qualitative results and comparisons with 3D-VisTA illustrate robustness to occlusion, rare objects, small targets, and cluttered scenes, supporting the quantitative findings.
The high-level idea is simple and practical: using panoramas as a bridge between 2D VLMs and 3D grounding is well motivated and could inspire further work.
weaknesses: The proposed Earth Mover's Distance loss is not a true numeric EMD over bounding-box coordinates. It treats each decimal digit as an independent categorical distribution and applies place-value weights, which ignores carry effects and makes the 'distance-aware' theoretical justification weaker than claimed.

Several evaluations, including ReferIt3D, cross-dataset generalization, and text-variant robustness, rely on ground-truth object proposals or segmentations. These settings primarily test candidate ranking/selection given oracle proposals rather than full 3D bounding-box grounding, so the reported gains may overstate end-to-end 3D grounding ability.

The method depends on multiple large external models and data assumptions: CogVLM-17B, DINOv2, SAM, original RGB-D views, and capture trajectories for semantic feature lifting and camera placement. This limits applicability to scenes without such captures and makes the pipeline computationally heavy (~3.3s per query on an A100).

The ablation for geometric features is somewhat ambiguous: adding geometric input without geometric QA slightly decreases accuracy (60.4 to 60.2), and the full model improves only +0.3 over the geometric-QA-without-geometry variant. The benefit of the geometric modality is therefore not fully isolated.

The multi-view 3D aggregation contains several heuristic components, including denoising, best-view selection, visibility filtering, AABB fitting, and SAM-based mask extraction. The sensitivity and failure modes of these components, especially SAM on distorted panoramic images, are not analyzed in depth.

The paper mainly reports ScanRefer Acc@0.25 and omits Acc@0.5, reducing comparability with standard ScanRefer evaluations that often report both. Some tables also compare numbers under different protocols (e.g., Table 2 Ours ScanRefer 64.9 vs. Table 1 61.0/62.0) without fully clarifying the setting differences.

The modified text queries are generated by LLaMA 3.3 and not human-validated. While useful as a robustness probe, they may not fully reflect natural paraphrase or affordance distributions, so the text-generalization claim should be interpreted with care.
No code release or project page is mentioned, and the method relies on many implementation details, which may hinder reproducibility despite the detailed supplement.

strengths: The paper proposes a simple and effective idea: using panoramic renderings as a 2D-3D interface so that pretrained 2D VLMs can be reused for 3D visual grounding. This is practically attractive because it preserves 360-degree scene context and avoids the limited field of view of perspective-image VLM pipelines.

The method is a complete and well-engineered pipeline: structure-aware camera placement, multi-modal panoramic rendering, a lightweight adapter for injecting geometric and semantic features into a VLM, visibility-aware 3D aggregation, an EMD loss for numeric supervision, and auxiliary geometric QA training.

Experiments are extensive and largely convincing. PanoGrounder achieves state-of-the-art or top-2 results on ScanRefer, Nr3D, and Sr3D, with particularly strong gains on human-written Nr3D queries, and further shows zero-shot promise, cross-dataset generalization, and robustness to text perturbations.

The ablations are broad: input modalities, EMD loss, geometric QA, camera placement factors, number of cameras, adapter layer placement, scene representations, test-time augmentation, and per-category/elevation analysis. This gives useful insight into which components matter.
Qualitative results and failure-case analyses are included, and the paper honestly discusses limitations such as reconstruction dependence, inference speed, and restricted query types.

Clarity is generally good. The main paper describes the pipeline clearly, and the supplementary material provides substantial implementation details, prompt templates, hyperparameters, and additional analyses, which improves reproducibility.

The work is potentially impactful for robotics, AR, and embodied AI because it suggests a practical way to leverage modern VLMs for 3D grounding without designing task-specific 3D tokens or training 3D encoders from scratch.
The deployment experiment on a self-captured scene, while limited, is a useful step toward demonstrating practical viability beyond clean benchmark meshes.
weaknesses: The algorithmic novelty is limited. The core idea of using panoramas to bridge 2D VLMs and 3D grounding is intuitive, and the method relies heavily on off-the-shelf components such as CogVLM, SAM, DINOv2, Mask3D, RANSAC, PyTorch3D, and ODGS. The contribution is more a well-executed system/pipeline than a fundamentally new formulation.

The method depends strongly on high-quality 3D reconstruction. Main results use mesh-rendered panoramas or cleaned 3D scenes, while fully automated reconstruction (3DGS*) drops to 55.1 from 61.6 and excludes many ScanNet scenes because COLMAP fails to register enough images. This weakens the claim that the approach relaxes 3D input requirements and is broadly practical.

Several evaluations use oracle-like 3D information. Generalization experiments use GT object masks, the ReferIt3D two-stage variant relies on GT candidate point cloud segments, and some ablations use GT segmentation. These choices isolate 2D grounding performance but are not fully end-to-end 3D visual grounding and may favor the method relative to point-cloud baselines.

Fairness of comparison is not fully controlled. Baselines differ in input representation (point clouds vs. rendered meshes/panoramas), training data (single-dataset vs. multi-dataset), and backbone capacity. Some baseline results are re-run by the authors, while others are cited; this makes it difficult to attribute gains purely to the proposed representation.

The computational cost is substantial. Offline per-scene processing includes COLMAP (~87 min), 3DGS training (~43 min), semantic feature lifting (~24 min), and rendering, while online inference uses a 17B VLM at ~3.3s per query and ~51.6 GB GPU memory. This is heavy for real-time robotics or large-scale deployment, and the efficiency analysis covers only a single self-captured scene.

Some component gains are modest or mixed. EMD, geometric feature injection, geometric QA, and adapter layer placement produce small improvements (e.g., adapter placement varies only between 60.9 and 61.0), and the paper does not report variance across seeds or statistical significance. More rigorous disentangling of contributions would strengthen the empirical case.

The panoramic representation has inherent limitations: equirectangular distortion, a floor-based grid that assumes a single indoor floor plane, limited vertical field of view, and no evaluation on outdoor, multi-floor, or dynamic scenes. The authors acknowledge some of these, but they remain important open issues for the claimed generalizability.

The text-generalization experiments use LLaMA-generated paraphrases and affordance variants. While the trend is interesting, especially on +Aff.-N, the mechanism behind the large relative improvement is not deeply analyzed, and generated text may not reflect real user language distributions.

The paper does not release code or checkpoints in the main text, and reproducibility details such as random seeds and training variance are missing. Although the supplementary material is helpful, full reproduction of the 17B-VLM and reconstruction pipeline remains non-trivial.

The state-of-the-art claim should be qualified. Because different methods use different input assumptions, backbones, and training protocols, the reported improvements establish strong performance on the chosen benchmarks but not necessarily dominance across the full 3DVG design space.

strengths: Introduces panoramic renderings as a 2D-3D interface for VLM-based 3D visual grounding, enabling direct use of pretrained 2D VLMs while preserving 360-degree scene context; the pinhole-vs-panorama ablation and qualitative comparisons support the central claim.

Reports strong empirical results on established benchmarks: state-of-the-art or top-2 performance on ScanRefer and Nr3D under single- and multi-dataset training, with particularly large gains on Nr3D and multi-object ScanRefer splits.

Provides an extensive experimental suite, including zero-shot comparisons, cross-dataset scene generalization, text-modification robustness, input and objective ablations, camera-placement analysis, mesh vs. 3DGS studies, efficiency measurements, and a real-world self-captured deployment.

Method components are thoughtfully motivated: structure-aware camera placement, multi-modal adapters with zero-convolution initialization, an EMD-style auxiliary digit loss, and visibility-aware multi-view 3D aggregation.
The paper is generally clear, well-illustrated, and includes substantial implementation details and prompts in the supplementary material, aiding reproducibility.
weaknesses: The main SOTA comparison is confounded by backbone scale: CogVLM-17B is much larger than most baselines, and the Qwen2.5-VL-7B variant (52.1) falls below several baselines such as PQ3D (57.0), LIBA (59.6), and VGMamba (60.0). Thus, the claim that gains stem largely from the panoramic design rather than backbone capacity alone is not fully supported.

Generalization claims are overstated in the abstract: cross-dataset results rely on ground-truth object segmentation for all methods, which evaluates selection among GT instances rather than end-to-end 3D grounding. This qualification appears in the experiments but not prominently in the abstract or introduction.

Training excludes panoramic views where the target object is not visible, yet test-time behavior when the target is invisible from all selected viewpoints is not analyzed. This may overstate practical robustness and leaves an important failure mode unquantified.

The visibility-aware 3D aggregation is a central component but is not ablated. The individual contributions of anchor-view selection, outlier removal, visibility filtering, and SAM-based mask lifting are not quantitatively validated, making the source of performance gains less transparent.

The zero-shot Nr3D comparison likely uses the two-stage variant with ground-truth candidates, but this is not clearly stated in the table. Fairness relative to fully end-to-end zero-shot methods such as SeeGround and VLM-Grounder is therefore unclear.

The EMD loss is applied digit-wise to discretized coordinates with place-value weights, which is not a true distance metric over numeric coordinates and can over-penalize boundary errors. Its measured benefit is modest (roughly 0.9-1.1 Acc@0.25).

Main results depend on high-quality mesh renderings and a 17B VLM, making the approach computationally heavy and less accessible. The automated 3DGS* variant drops substantially (61.6 to 55.1 on the evaluated subset), indicating sensitivity to reconstruction quality.

strengths: Proposes a simple but effective panoramic 2D-3D interface that lets a pretrained 2D VLM operate on 360-degree renderings, preserving long-range spatial context while avoiding perspective view-direction prediction.

The method is carefully designed and well-motivated: structure-aware camera placement, multi-modal panoramic renderings (RGB, range, semantic features), lightweight adapters, EMD-based coordinate supervision, and visibility-aware 3D aggregation.

Extensive empirical validation: strong results on ScanRefer, Nr3D, and Sr3D, plus cross-dataset generalization on ARKitScenes+SceneVerse and 3RScan+RIORefer. Text-robustness experiments, especially the +Aff.-N and Mask settings, show meaningful language-reasoning gains.

The supplementary material provides substantial reproducibility detail, including camera placement, rendering configuration, adapter placement, hyperparameters, prompts, efficiency measurements, real-world deployment, and failure-case analysis.

Ablations and qualitative results support the main claims: panorama vs. pinhole comparisons, modality ablations, camera placement analysis, and mesh vs. 3DGS comparisons help isolate the contribution of the panoramic representation.
weaknesses: The main benchmark results rely on mesh-rendered panoramas from dataset reconstructions, while the fully automated raw-RGB pipeline is only supplementary and evaluated on a subset (3DGS* at 55.1 Acc@0.25). The practical claim of requiring only casually captured RGB frames is therefore not fully supported in the main setting, and preprocessing is expensive (COLMAP 87 min, 3DGS 43 min, semantic lifting 24 min).

Headline comparisons are partly confounded by backbone capacity: PanoGrounder uses a 17B CogVLM, while many 3DVG baselines are trained from scratch with much smaller encoders. Although backbone-scaling and pinhole controls are provided, the direct SOTA numbers are not purely attributable to the panoramic representation.

Several ablation gains are small and reported without variance or statistical significance, e.g., EMD adds roughly 0.9-1.1 points and the geometric/semantic synergy is only around 0.3-0.6 points. Claims about component contributions and synergy may be overinterpreted.

The zero-shot setup is not fully specified: it is unclear whether the adapters and semantic features are used without any fine-tuning, or whether the zero-shot results come from the base VLM with only panoramic RGB. This makes the comparison to larger VLM baselines harder to interpret.

The 3D aggregation stage depends on off-the-shelf SAM and heuristic anchor-view selection/filtering, but there is no ablation or sensitivity analysis of these choices. Since aggregation is central to converting 2D predictions into 3D boxes, its robustness is under-examined.

There are minor reproducibility inconsistencies, e.g., supplementary ScanRefer mesh accuracy is 61.6 while the main table reports 61.0, and no code release is mentioned. These do not invalidate the contribution but slightly weaken full reproducibility.
